title: Malthusian theory
recall_points: Population grows geometrically; food production arithmetically → population outstrips subsistence resources → Malthusian catastrophe in the diagram
Time on horizontal axis; quantity on vertical axis
Population curve accelerates; resources increase linearly

title: Demographic transition diagram
recall_points: High stationary: high birth/death rates, low increase
Early expanding: death rate falls while births stay high
Late expanding: birth rate declines, growth slows
Possible declining stage: births below deaths, natural decrease
Deaths fall + births remain high → wider births–deaths gap → natural increase → rapid expansion
Births can remain above deaths while declining → positive natural increase persists → population still grows, more slowly
Later stages: base narrows, middle/older cohorts expand
Declining stage: smaller young cohorts relative to middle/older ages

title: Births, deaths and migration
recall_points: Total change = births − deaths + net migration
CBR: live births per 1,000 people per year
CDR: deaths per 1,000 people per year
Immigration/emigration change the population too → add net migration

title: Infant mortality
recall_points: Early pregnancy/inadequate maternal care + birth complications/infections → risk
Timely newborn care, nutrition and immunisation address these risks

title: Maternal mortality
recall_points: Early pregnancy and restricted reproductive decisions create additional risk → health services and autonomy both matter

title: Fertility and replacement
recall_points: TFR: average children born to a woman over her lifetime
Replacement level: fertility at which one generation replaces the previous generation
Male-selective migration → urban population has more men → altered sex composition → lower TFR, as stated in the slide
Single asterisk → below replacement level of 2.1

title: Sex ratio and dependency
recall_points: Child sex ratio: girls per 1,000 boys in the 0–6 age group
Kerala: male-selective outmigration → higher female/male ratio
Haryana: male-selective immigration → lower female/male ratio
Christian and tribal belts have better sex ratios

title: India’s demographic-growth phases
recall_points: Stagnant → high birth and death rates
